prompt: Why does the shop alert on checkout failures with a log search alert rather than a metric alert?
hint: Which signal knows which requests failed?

choices.text: Metric alerts cannot have a severity
choices.why: Both kinds have one.

choices.text: Only the logs know which route failed
choices.why: Right. A platform metric counts 5xx for the whole app; the query can single out checkout.

choices.text: Log search alerts fire faster than metric alerts
choices.why: The reverse: logs arrive in minutes, metrics are evaluated every minute.

choices.text: Metric alerts are billed per request
choices.why: Rules are billed per rule and per frequency, not per request.

prompt: Match each setting of a log search alert to what it decides.

pairs.right: How far back each run looks
How many yes answers in a row before firing

prompt: A stateless rule (no autoMitigate) evaluates every 5 minutes through a 40-minute incident. What does on-call receive?
hint: Every yes is a new alert.

choices.text: One alert, resolved at the end
choices.why: That is the stateful behaviour.

choices.text: Nothing at all until the incident has ended
choices.why: Alerts fire during the condition, not after.

choices.text: About eight alerts, one per evaluation
choices.why: Right. That is why the shop turns autoMitigate on.

choices.text: One alert per failed request in the window
choices.why: Alerts come from evaluations of the query, not from each row.

choices.text: So a quiet night pages nobody
choices.why: Right. One in three is 33% and means nothing.

choices.text: Kusto refuses percentages over fewer than ten rows
choices.why: It computes any percentage; the guard is a design choice.

choices.text: Log search alerts need at least ten rows to run
choices.why: They run on any result, including none.

choices.text: Ten is the default failing-periods setting
choices.why: Failing periods count evaluations, not requests.

prompt: According to evaluate.kql, when would checkout-failing have fired, in São Paulo time?
hint: The first window to say yes ended at 17:10 UTC.

choices.text: 14:05, the moment the incident began
choices.why: The rule needs a window to end before it can see it.
Right. 17:10 UTC, and a few minutes later in a real workspace, where logs arrive late.

choices.text: 17:10, because alerts use São Paulo time
choices.why: 17:10 is UTC; São Paulo is three hours behind.

choices.text: 14:55, when it resolved
choices.why: That is the resolution, not the firing.

prompt: In the window ending 17:25, what percentage of checkouts failed?
hint: 9 of 22, rounded to the nearest whole number.

prompt: A colleague proposes raising the threshold from 5% to 50% to avoid noise. What does Thursday's table say would happen?

choices.text: The alert would fire once and resolve at the end
choices.why: 17:25 was at 41%, so it would resolve mid-incident.

choices.text: It would never fire at all during Thursday's incident
choices.why: Most windows were above 60%.

choices.text: It would resolve at 17:25 and fire again at 17:30
choices.why: Right. A high threshold turns one incident into two alerts.

choices.text: It would fire earlier, at 17:05
choices.why: A higher threshold can only fire later or the same.

prompt: Twelve alert rules should all page the on-call engineer. What does the action group buy the team?
hint: Count the edits when the rota changes.

choices.text: Cheaper e-mails
choices.why: Price is not why.

choices.text: Faster evaluation of all twelve rules
choices.why: Action groups act after firing; they do not evaluate.

choices.text: One place to change who is paged
choices.why: Right. Twelve rules name one group; one edit changes all of them.

choices.text: Automatic suppression of alerts at night
choices.why: That is a processing rule's job.

prompt: What does `useCommonAlertSchema: true` change for the shop's chat webhook?
hint: Metric and log alerts arrive in what shape?

choices.text: It encrypts the payload
choices.why: HTTPS protects it in transit; the schema is about shape.

choices.text: Every kind of alert arrives in one JSON shape
choices.why: Right. The consumer understands one format instead of several.

choices.text: It limits the webhook to alerts of severity 0 and 1
choices.why: Severity filtering is not what the schema does.

choices.text: It turns the webhook into an e-mail
choices.why: Each receiver keeps its type.

prompt: During planned maintenance, why does the shop suppress notifications instead of disabling checkout-failing?
hint: What does a disabled rule record?

choices.text: Disabled rules are still billed
choices.why: Cost is not the argument.

choices.text: Rules cannot be disabled once deployed
choices.why: They can; `enabled: false` does it.

choices.text: The alert is still recorded
choices.why: Right. A disabled rule leaves no trace and is easily forgotten.

choices.text: Processing rules page a different team instead
choices.why: This one removes all action groups; it pages nobody.

prompt: The maintenance window was written with timeZone UTC and the same 02:00 to 04:00. What happens on the night?
hint: 02:00 UTC is what time in São Paulo?

choices.text: Nothing changes; Azure converts to local time
choices.why: The schedule is read in the zone it names.

choices.text: It silences 23:00 to 01:00 and pages at 02:05
choices.why: Right. The window lands three hours early in local time.

choices.text: The processing rule fails to deploy
choices.why: UTC is a valid zone; it deploys and is wrong.

choices.text: It silences 05:00 to 07:00
choices.why: São Paulo is behind UTC, not ahead.

prompt: Put what happens at 17:10 UTC on Thursday in order, from the rule's point of view.
items: It returns a row, so the condition is met
Processing rules are applied to it
ag-shop-oncall e-mails and posts to chat
trap: Putting the action group before the processing rules is the slip: they sit between the alert and its receivers.

prompt: Which of these did this lesson actually run? Choose all that apply.
hint: Compile and query, yes; fire and send, no.

choices.text: Compiling the alert rule, the action group and the processing rule
choices.why: Yes. bicep build, all three.

choices.text: The rule's query over each five-minute window of Thursday
choices.why: Yes. evaluate.kql in the emulator.

choices.text: An e-mail to oncall@example.com
choices.why: No. Nothing was deployed, and example.com belongs to nobody.

choices.text: Suppressing a real alert during maintenance
choices.why: No. There were no alerts to suppress.
